name: logit
title: Generalized logit and inverse logit function

origin.description: Generalized logit. Values on [min, max] map to the real line.

arguments.name: min
arguments.text: Lower end of the logit interval.

arguments.name: max
arguments.text: Upper end of the logit interval.

origin.details: p = (x - min) / (max - min) and the result is log(p / (1 - p)). An endpoint is infinite. A finite value outside the interval is NaN, and log warns once. min and max follow ordinary arithmetic recycling.
origin.example:
x <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.25)
xt <- logit(x, min = 0, max = 10)
cbind(x, xt)

translation.description: Generalized logit. Values on [min, max] map to the real line.

arguments.name: min
arguments.text: Lower end of the logit interval.

arguments.name: max
arguments.text: Upper end of the logit interval.

translation.details: p = (x - min) / (max - min) and the result is log(p / (1 - p)). An endpoint is infinite. A finite value outside the interval is NaN, and log warns once. min and max follow ordinary arithmetic recycling. A Python int is a double, matching a numeric literal. An int32 vector uses 32-bit subtraction.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from gtools.logit import logit
x = np.arange(41) / 4
xt = logit(x, min=0, max=10)
print(np.column_stack((x, xt)))
